    Aperiodic Garden

    A garden laid out on the hat — the 13-sided einstein monotile that tiles the plane and never repeats. Three hats pinwheel around a snow-capped peak; a river runs off it.

    • Move the mouse near a light. The hat turns itself to a way it fits there.
    • Tap near a light. The hat turns itself to a way it fits there.
    • Scroll (or Q/E) to cycle the other ways — twelve orientations, mirrored ones included.
    • ⟲ ⟳ cycle the other ways — twelve orientations, mirrored ones included.
    • Click to lay it. Covers may meet however they like; only two things are forbidden — walling in a stream, and leaving a gap no hat could ever fill.
    • Tap it again, or press Place, to lay it. Covers may meet however they like; only two things are forbidden — walling in a stream, and leaving a gap no hat could ever fill.
    • Ring a meadow, forest, hills, hamlet or scree completely and it seals: big points, and more tiles.
    • A mill stands off across the grass with a dry leat. Carry the headwater to it — two or three stream tiles — and its wheel starts turning.
    • Everything you build works: a turning wheel grinds, a woodcutter's camp cuts timber. Spend what they make at the workshop for a tile you chose rather than one you were dealt — up to the water works, which goes anywhere and takes up every stream it lands against.
    • Drag to look round; two fingers zoom, pan and turn the garden.

    The garden behind this card is laying itself. Yours starts from the peak.
